chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man complained to him about the epidemic, so he said to him: 'And where are you from the good, the Blessed?' He said, 'I said, 'And what is the good, the Blessed?'' So he said: 'Your Suleymaniyya (sugar), this.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The first one to take the sugar was Suleyman ibn Dawood (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُد: Suleyman ibn Dawood (Prophet Solomon son of David)
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانِيُّكُمْ: Your Suleymaniyya (a specific type/variety of sugar)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sugar in Shia hadith and who was the first to use it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes 'Suleymaniyya'—a specific variety of sugar—as a remedy for the plague, identifying it as 'the good, the Blessed.' The Imam links this medicinal practice to Prophet Suleyman (peace be upon him), establishing a historical precedent for sugar's therapeutic use in Shia tradition. This highlights the Islamic emphasis on utilizing natural substances for health, rooted in prophetic wisdom.
